title: walkbench: Testbed of Walking Models for the Divergence Exponents of Gait

creators.name: Terrier, Philippe
creators.affiliation: Haute Ecole Arc Santé, HES-SO University of Applied Sciences and Arts Western Switzerland, Neuchâtel, Switzerland

description: Walking models share a common interface, so that an experiment written for one model runs on the others without change. The interface has a perturbation port that accepts any input series, a closed-loop port for corrective controllers and a metronome, and a linearization at the fixed point. Runs have standardized outputs, and a run driver applies a seed rule, redraws a run after a fall and writes a run log. Common estimators compute the short-term and long-term divergence exponents with the Rosenstein engine of RACING v1.0.2 (Terrier 2026, doi:10.5281/zenodo.20542521), the Floquet multipliers, the kinematic variability and the scaling exponent of detrended fluctuation analysis. The package contains two models. M1 is the simplest walking model of Garcia et al. (1998, doi:10.1115/1.2798313), perturbed at each foot strike as in Su and Dingwell (2007, doi:10.1115/1.2800760). M2 is the walking model with arced feet and a hip spring of Hobbelen and Wisse (2007, doi:10.1109/TRO.2007.904908), as used by Bruijn et al. (2012, doi:10.1016/j.medengphy.2011.07.024). Its input is the height of the floor at each step. The campaign rules follow the analysis plan of the SIM-ACI project, registered on OSF Registries (doi:10.17605/OSF.IO/M74TK). They cover the master seeds, the transients, the rescaling of the inputs, the real stride series and their surrogates, and the fall rate of each cell. An analytic predictor gives the expected divergence curve and the long-term exponent from the linearization of a model and the autocovariance of its input. The folder docs/ of the repository holds the user guide of version 0.7.0 in PDF and the example scripts that produced it. The folder web/ holds a simulator of the models M1 and M2 for a web browser.
